o: The apostle salutes the elect lady and her children.
Express his joy in their faith and love.
bg: Is addressed to "the elect lady," and closes with the words, "The children of thy elect sister greet thee;" but some would read instead of "lady" the proper name Kyria. Of the thirteen verses composing this epistle seven are in the First Epistle.
ch.s: This chapter covers: The apostle salutes the elect lady and her children (vv. 1–3); Express his joy in their faith and love (vv. 4–6); Cautions them against deceivers (vv. 7–11); And concludes (vv. 12,13).
ch.mh: Religion turns compliments into real expressions of respect and love.
q: Read verses 1–3 (The apostle salutes the elect lady and her children). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 4–6 (Express his joy in their faith and love), what do you learn about love?
Verse 9 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside John 7:16–17. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
Where do you see the theme of truth and light in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of 2 John?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: Yet in obeying this command, we must show kindness and a good spirit to those who differ from us in lesser matters, but hold firmly the all-important doctrines of Christ's person, atonement, and holy salvation.
ch.a: Do one concrete, unannounced act of love for someone in your home or church.
